query: Consider the following context: The recent trend of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) was studied extensively for their promising mechanical properties, but individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored. In that context, which method can be used for the effects of changing the percentage of elements of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA on the mechanical properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Systematic variations in the elemental percentages of the HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy will lead to measurable changes in mechanical properties due to altered lattice distortion and phase stability.
generation.material_initial_state: An equiatomic, single-phase HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy produced by conventional casting or sputtering methods.
generation.intervention: Vary the percentage of one or more constituents in the alloy using a high‐throughput combinatorial synthesis method combined with a design‐of‐experiments approach.
generation.conditions: Samples are processed under identical thermal treatment (e.g., homogenization and annealing) and tested at room temperature to isolate composition effects.
generation.structural_mediator: Changes in elemental concentration modify the lattice distortion and can induce subtle variations in microstructure, such as grain size and secondary phase formation.
generation.mechanism: Altering the relative amounts of the constituent elements changes the degree of solid solution strengthening and may affect dislocation mobility, thereby altering mechanical properties like yield strength and hardness.
generation.predicted_outcome: Increasing the percentage of specific elements (for example, adjusting Hf or Ta beyond the equiatomic ratio) is expected to enhance strength and hardness due to increased lattice distortion, while other adjustments may reduce ductility or lead to phase separation if the single-phase region is exceeded.
generation.baseline: The equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy serves as the baseline for comparison.
generation.boundary: The predictions are valid as long as the compositional variations remain within the single-phase regime. Exceeding the boundaries may result in the formation of secondary phases that complicate the mechanical behavior.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude and non-linear nature of the mechanical property changes are uncertain and will depend on the precise processing conditions and the interplay between different strengthening mechanisms.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of HfNbTaTiZr alloy samples with systematically varied compositions using a combinatorial synthesis technique. Maintain identical processing and heat-treatment conditions for all samples. Characterize the microstructure and phase composition using X-ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), then measure mechanical properties (e.g., yield strength, hardness) using standard testing methods.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no systematic relationship is found between the compositional variations and the mechanical properties beyond measurement uncertainty—or if improvements in mechanical properties do not correlate with the intended changes in lattice distortion or phase stability—the hypothesis is falsified.
